output.myth: Vesket was a goods boat with a salt cargo for the islands, and her captain was a careful woman who counted every sack before the lines were cast. One winter Tavo the Gale came up under her and laughed, and the hull went to pieces on the reef. The sacks went down into the dark water, and the captain went down after them, still counting. Orrun felt the weight go over his back and sighed, and Kael cast his net for the sacks, as he always does, and caught nothing. So the captain is still down there, one bag, then one more, and the lamp at her bow is the last salt she carried. Mothers say a sailor who loses a bag should not curse the sea; she only adds it to her count. When the wind is kind, Hesk lets one sack drift up toward the Lamp Road, and the children on the cliffs count it aloud.
output.verse:
Salt in the bow-lamp,
Vesket counts her sacks in dark,
one bag, then one more.
